claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 exhibits a hierarchical heterostructure containing nanoprecipitates and intra- and intergranular features.
The hierarchical nanoprecipitate distribution in HfNbTiVAl10 mediates dislocation interactions.
Phase interfaces in HfNbTiVAl10 mediate crack initiation.
Phase interfaces in HfNbTiVAl10 mediate crack propagation.
Adding experimentally measured hierarchical microstructural descriptors will improve the accuracy of Young's modulus predictions.
Adding experimentally measured hierarchical microstructural descriptors will improve the accuracy of yield-strength predictions.
Adding experimentally measured hierarchical microstructural descriptors will improve the accuracy of fracture-behavior predictions.
The machine-learning-enhanced multiscale framework will make the mechanical-property predictions faster than conventional simulations.
The machine-learning module will reduce the need for extensive high-fidelity simulations.
The integrated framework will quickly approximate stress distributions.
The integrated framework will quickly approximate failure mechanisms.
The framework may improve correlation with experimental measurements by 20–30%.
The framework may reduce simulation time by 30–50%.
Conventional finite-element or atomistic simulations generally do not explicitly incorporate detailed hierarchical structural data.
Conventional simulation methods are slower than the proposed framework.
Conventional simulation methods are less accurate at capturing the effects of hierarchical heterostructures.
Insufficient imaging resolution may prevent the proposed framework from improving predictions.
Failure of the machine-learning model to generalize across scales may prevent improved predictions.
The framework may be less effective for dynamic fracture at very high strain rates.
The framework may be less effective for alloys with substantially different microstructural complexity.
